questions.text:
Consider the following grammar.

P[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]xQRS
Q[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]yz|z
R[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]w|[latex]\varepsilon[/latex]
S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]y

What is FOLLOW (Q) ?
questions.solution:
In [latex]P\rightarrow xQRS[/latex], Q is followed by RS. FIRST(R) = {w, [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]}, so FOLLOW(Q) gets w, and since R can vanish, FIRST(S) = {y} too.

FOLLOW(Q) = {w, y}

Answer: {w, y}

questions.text:
Consider the following context-free grammar over the alphabet [latex]\sum[/latex] = {a,b,c} with S as the start symbol.

S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]abScT|abcT
T[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]bT|b

Which one of the following represents the language generated by the above grammar ?
questions.solution:
Each use of [latex]S\rightarrow abScT[/latex] adds an "ab" on the left and a "cT" on the right; the last step [latex]S\rightarrow abcT[/latex] adds one more pair. T gives [latex]b^m[/latex] with m [latex]\ge[/latex] 1, chosen separately each time.

So: [latex](ab)^n\,cb^{m_1}cb^{m_2}\ldots cb^{m_n}[/latex] with all [latex]m_i\ge1[/latex].

Answer: Option 2

questions.text:
What is the highest type number that can be assigned to the following grammar?
[latex]S \rightarrow A a, A \rightarrow B a, B \rightarrow a b c[/latex]
questions.solution:
Every rule has at most one non-terminal, always at the left end of the right side ([latex]S\rightarrow Aa[/latex], [latex]A\rightarrow Ba[/latex], [latex]B\rightarrow abc[/latex]). That is a left-linear grammar, which is regular: Type 3.

Answer: Type 3

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
[latex]S \rightarrow a S a|b S b| a \mid b[/latex]
The language generated by the above grammar over the alphabet {a,b} is the set of:
questions.solution:
Each step adds the same symbol at both ends, and the derivation ends with a single a or b in the middle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] odd-length palindromes (all of them).

Answer: all odd length palindromes

questions.text: If [latex]L[/latex] and [latex]\bar L[/latex] are recursively enumerable then [latex]L[/latex] is
questions.solution:
Run the recognizers of L and [latex]\bar L[/latex] in parallel on input w. Exactly one of them accepts, so the procedure always halts with the right answer [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] L is recursive.

Answer: recursive
